Acute rheumatic fever can occur without heart involvement or with heart involvement, which may manifest as acute rheumatic pericarditis, endocarditis, myocarditis, or other acute rheumatic heart diseases. Rheumatic chorea is another possible manifestation. 2. Chronic rheumatic heart diseases include conditions affecting the mitral, aortic, and tricuspid valves, such as mitral stenosis, mitral insufficiency, aortic stenosis, aortic insufficiency, and tricuspid stenosis or insufficiency. Multiple valve disorders and other chronic rheumatic heart diseases, such as myocarditis or chronic pericarditis, may also occur. 3.g., hypertensive nephropathy), combined hypertensive heart and renal disease, and secondary hypertension, such as renovascular hypertension. 4. Ischemic heart diseases encompass angina pectoris (e.g., unstable angina, Prinzmetal's angina), acute myocardial infarction, subsequent myocardial infarction, complications following myocardial infarction (e.g., haemopericardium, septal defects, cardiac wall rupture, or thrombosis), other acute ischemic heart diseases (e.g., coronary thrombosis or Dressler's syndrome), and chronic ischemic heart diseases (e.g., atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, old myocardial infarction, ischemic cardiomyopathy, or silent myocardial ischemia). 5. Pulmonary heart diseases and diseases of pulmonary circulation include pulmonary embolism, primary pulmonary hypertension, secondary pulmonary hypertension, kyphoscoliotic heart disease, and other pulmonary vascular diseases, such as arteriovenous fistula or pulmonary artery aneurysm. 6. Pericardial diseases include acute pericarditis, chronic adhesive or constrictive pericarditis, haemopericardium, pericardial effusion, and cardiac tamponade. Pericarditis may also occur in association with other diseases. 7. Endocardial diseases include acute and subacute endocarditis, nonrheumatic mitral valve disorders (e.g., mitral insufficiency, mitral prolapse, or mitral stenosis), nonrheumatic aortic valve disorders (e.g., aortic stenosis or insufficiency), nonrheumatic tricuspid valve disorders, and pulmonary valve disorders. Endocarditis may also occur in association with other diseases. 8. Myocardial diseases include acute myocarditis, myocarditis associated with other diseases, and cardiomyopathies, such as dilated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, restrictive cardiomyopathy, endomyocardial disease (e.g., Löffler's endocarditis), and alcoholic cardiomyopathy. 9. Disorders of the heart's electrical conduction system include atrioventricular and bundle-branch blocks (e.g., first-degree, second-degree, or complete atrioventricular block), fascicular blocks, nonspecific intraventricular blocks, pre-excitation syndromes (e.g., Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome), and other conduction disorders (e.g., long QT syndrome or Stokes-Adams syndrome). 10. Cardiac arrhythmias include paroxysmal tachycardia (e.g., supraventricular or ventricular tachycardia), atrial fibrillation and flutter, ventricular fibrillation, premature depolarizations, sick sinus syndrome, and other specified or unspecified arrhythmias. 11. Heart failure may present as congestive heart failure or other forms of heart failure. Complications and ill-defined heart diseases include myocarditis, cardiomegaly (e.g., ventricular hypertrophy), and unspecified cardiovascular diseases. 12. Cerebrovascular diseases include subarachnoid hemorrhage (e.g., from specific intracranial arteries), intracerebral hemorrhage (e.g., subcortical, cortical, or brainstem), nontraumatic intracranial hemorrhage (e.g., subdural or extradural), cerebral infarction (e.g., due to thrombosis or embolism), stroke (unspecified as hemorrhagic or ischemic), and occlusion or stenosis of cerebral or precerebral arteries. Other cerebrovascular conditions include cerebral aneurysms, atherosclerosis, hypertensive encephalopathy, Moyamoya disease, and cerebral arteritis. 13. Diseases of arteries, arterioles, and capillaries include atherosclerosis, aortic aneurysms and dissections, peripheral vascular diseases (e.g., Raynaud's syndrome or thromboangiitis obliterans), arterial embolism or thrombosis, and other disorders such as arterial fibromuscular dysplasia or necrosis. Capillary diseases include hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia and non-neoplastic naevi. 14. Diseases of veins, lymphatic vessels, and lymph nodes include phlebitis and thrombophlebitis (e.g., deep vein thrombosis), portal vein thrombosis, venous embolism or thrombosis (e.g., Budd-Chiari syndrome), varicose veins, hemorrhoids, and venous insufficiency. Lymphatic disorders include lymphedema, lymphangitis, and other noninfective lymphatic conditions. 15. Other circulatory system disorders include hypotension (e.g., orthostatic or drug-induced), postprocedural circulatory disorders, and other unspecified circulatory conditions.
